title: From Traits to Behaviours: What Effectiveness Really Means
brief: Open the unit by establishing that effective teaching is best understood through observable classroom behaviours rather than fixed personality traits. Draw on the module's framing of teacher observation as a tool for evaluating practice — specifically the 'observe, evaluate, adapt, act' cycle described in the introduction to Shaping the Way We Teach English: From Observation to Action. Explain that the unit will examine concrete actions teachers take before, during, and after lessons, and that these actions — not innate qualities — are what trainees can learn, practice, and improve.

title: Preparation and Clear Objectives
brief: Focus on lesson preparation as a foundation of effective teaching, centred on the module's repeated emphasis on lesson objectives and assessment. Draw directly on the observation questions that ask trainees to describe lesson objectives and explain how a teacher evaluates whether those objectives were met — including both formal and informal assessment of student performance. Explain that a well-prepared teacher knows in advance what students should be able to do by the end of the lesson and builds in ways to check that learning has occurred, such as concept-checking questions and comprehension checks described in the module.

title: Clarity in the Classroom: Instructions, Questions, and Checking Understanding
brief: Cover the behaviours through which effective teachers communicate clearly with learners. Draw on the module's discussion of giving directions at an appropriate pace with suitable vocabulary, gestures, and pausing; asking comprehension-checking questions such as 'How long do you have to answer the questions?'; and having students repeat directions back while the teacher writes them on the board. Also draw on the module's treatment of concept-checking questions as a tool for teaching vocabulary and verifying understanding, and the technique of asking all students — not just one — to display their knowledge.

title: Rapport and Fairness: Building an Inclusive Classroom
brief: Examine how effective teachers build positive relationships and treat all learners equitably. Draw on the module's discussion of physical proximity — the teacher sitting close to very young learners on the floor and the advantages this closeness offers — as a concrete rapport-building behavior. Use the module's emphasis on giving every student a chance to display knowledge and answer questions, including techniques such as think-pair-share, having one student call on another, and throwing a soft ball so multiple students respond in turn. Connect these behaviours to fairness: ensuring no single student dominates and that quieter or shyer students are encouraged to produce language.

title: Adaptability: Managing the Classroom and Responding to Learners
brief: Address adaptability as a set of in-the-moment classroom management behaviours rather than a personality trait. Draw on the module's detailed treatment of managing off-task students without disrupting lesson flow, using transitions between activities, establishing classroom routines that help students become more autonomous, and varying seating arrangements to suit different activity types. Include the module's examples of specific management techniques such as chants, signals for attention, and movement incorporated into activities. Emphasise that adaptability also means adjusting to the available classroom environment — for instance, adapting learning-station ideas when a classroom is not ideally equipped.

title: Reflection as a Professional Habit
brief: Close the unit by presenting reflection as a deliberate, recurring behavior that distinguishes effective teachers. Draw directly on the module's 'Reflecting and Adapting' sections, which ask teachers to consider what went well, what they might do differently, and what alternative approaches or strategies they could use in the future. Explain the 'observe, evaluate, adapt, act' cycle from the module's introduction as a practical framework trainees can apply after every lesson. Stress that reflection is not a one-time event but the starting point of the cycle again, and that keeping this habit is what allows teachers to continue improving their concrete classroom practice over time.
